operational-example.copy: Use Popover for short anchored context or local actions when Tooltip is too small and Dialog is too heavy.

scenario.title: Popover
scenario.meta: Show a short anchored contextual panel with optional local actions without becoming a drawer, dialog, form system, or option-layer pattern.
rationale: Use Popover for short anchored context or local actions when Tooltip is too small and Dialog is too heavy.
Popover can align to a full-width trigger on forms, but the panel remains short, anchored, and dismissible.
On small touch viewports, keep content short or escalate to Bottom Sheet when the panel needs room.

items.rule: Visible control that owns aria-expanded and opens the panel.
Anchored surface with short contextual content.
Keeps the panel visually connected to its trigger.
Uses concise text and optional local actions only.
Closes on Escape, outside interaction, or completed local action.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, warning, open, focus, hover, closed
items: Provide a visible accessible label for the control.
Expose current state and relationship through ARIA where applicable.
Support keyboard focus and expected dismissal or selection keys.
Do not rely on color alone for selected, warning, loading, or disabled state.
Escalate to a pattern when orchestration exceeds one component.

variants.copy: Popover variants describe anchored contextual surfaces; persistent panels, long forms, and option layers belong to other components or patterns.

states.copy: Popover states define closed, open, focus, warning, and disabled behavior around the trigger-panel pair.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant controls content shape; state controls visibility and priority without creating a process.

full-width.copy: Popover can align to a full-width trigger on forms, but the panel remains short, anchored, and dismissible.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: On small touch viewports, keep content short or escalate to Bottom Sheet when the panel needs room.

viewport-organization.copy: Viewport rules decide placement and escalation; Popover remains contextual, not persistent workspace.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use touch-safe targets and avoid covering critical content.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep the component close to the surface it controls.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact density only when labels and focus remain visible.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify trigger copy, variant, state, placement, and short content boundaries.

api-foundations.copy: Popover API exposes trigger, open state, placement, variant, state, and dismiss behavior while Design System owns focus, depth, and responsive escalation.

props.name: fullWidth
props.notes: Allows the trigger to align to a form row while keeping the panel contextual.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Disables the trigger and panel opening.

props.name: actions
props.type: Array<{ label: string, variant?: string, key?: string }>
props.notes: Optional local actions rendered with Button.

props.name: field
props.type: { label?: string, value?: string, placeholder?: string, helper?: string }
props.notes: Optional one-field local edit rendered with Input.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.notes: Called when local open state changes.

props.name: onAction
props.notes: Called when a local action is selected.

groups.title: Use
items: Use when Tooltip is too small for the content.
Anchor the panel to a visible trigger.
Keep content short and locally actionable.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not place long forms or processs inside Popover.
Do not use Popover as persistent detail panel.
Do not hide required instructions behind an optional trigger.

groups.title: Review
items: Check mobile escalation when space is tight.

rejectIf: Panel is detached from its trigger.
Required content is hidden without fallback.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Popover as anchored contextual disclosure. Agents may place it for short help or local actions, while humans confirm focus, dismissal, placement, and whether the content should escalate to a pattern.
canDecide: Use Popover for short contextual panels, local actions, metric explanations, and small anchored forms.
Escalate to Bottom Sheet on mobile when content needs more space.
Keep trigger, panel label, and dismissal rules explicit.
mustAsk: The content has multiple steps, long text, search, or complex forms.
The panel affects critical financial or safety decisions.
Placement may collide with navigation, maps, or sticky controls.
rejectIf: Panel is detached from its trigger.
Required content is hidden without fallback.
miel.handoff: I am using Popover for anchored contextual content. Please confirm trigger label, placement, dismissal, focus return, mobile escalation, and that this is not a persistent detail pattern.
